A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from AutoDS to AutoDiscovery. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original discovery experiments across 21 datasets, human evaluations, agent-validity audits and additional o4-mini experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and human-evaluation outcomes. The checklist's contradictory statements about human research do not negate the explicitly reported study.

M1.justification: Section 3, the algorithms and appendix prompts retain the same belief elicitation, surprisal-driven MCTS, progressive widening, discovery-agent workflow and HAC deduplication. AutoDiscovery is a renaming, without a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five DiscoveryBench datasets, 15 BLADE datasets and SEA-AD donor metadata. The human-study population and task coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: Repeated sampling, linear search, greedy search, beam search and the alternative reward comparisons are retained. The programmatic-search baseline also remains; its discussion moves from v1 Section 5.4 to v2 Section 9.5.

E3.justification: The 500-hypothesis budget, GPT-4o/o4-mini configurations, beam width and branching factor of 8, last-100 context and human-annotation sample counts and procedures remain unchanged. No evaluation-design revision is documented.

E4.justification: Reward substitutions, domain belief-shift analysis, uniqueness analysis, o4-mini comparisons, agent/deduplication audits and example outputs and errors are retained. The new limitations discussion supplies qualifications without adding an ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.1 first reports a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the retained 67% human-surprise estimate, using 10,000 resamples. v1 reports the point estimate without this interval. Additional independent experimental runs are not documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds the numerical confidence interval [0.63, 0.71] around the existing human-surprise estimate. Matched table values, plotted results, rankings and appendix outcomes otherwise remain unchanged, including the programmatic baseline's average of 109 unique surprisals.

T1.justification: The hypothesis and verification definitions, Beta belief estimates, Bayesian-surprise and belief-shift definitions, and UCT mathematics in Equations 1-6 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: surprise-guided open-ended discovery, 5-29% more LLM-surprising discoveries across 21 datasets, and approximately two-thirds agreement with expert surprise.

C2.justification: New Section 10 explicitly discusses execution-environment corruption, long-context failures, ungrounded attributes and the gap between LLM surprise and human novelty, suggesting literature-grounded extensions. These extend the retained latency and error discussions with specific applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The repository reference changes from allenai/autods to allenai/autodiscovery, and the new checklist adds code-sharing declarations. Existing prompts, Table 4 settings and runtime disclosures are retained. The PDFs do not establish actual repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introductory OpenAI/Google Deep Research footnote and associated references. It adds Gao et al. (2024) and a sentence connecting Bayesian surprise with mutual information in Section 6. The main research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 renames the system and title, updates affiliation/contact/header text, swaps Sections 5.1 and 5.2, moves the programmatic-search discussion, removes the contents pages and adds limitations and a NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose is preserved.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are reused, with Tables 1 and 2 exchanging numbers and several appendix figures relocated. Prompt/output blocks and page layouts reflow. Figure 6 in v2 partially obscures the Section 11.2 heading on page 22.

improvement.justification: The added bootstrap interval and specific limitations improve uncertainty disclosure and qualification of the unchanged findings. However, new checklist items 14-15 deny crowdsourcing and human research despite the retained paid Prolific study in Section 11. These gains coexist with a new reporting-consistency defect, leaving the net effect on overall paper quality unclear.
